title: Lesson 89: Your 90-day roadmap: hands-on practice plan, what to study next
description: Three applied questions on sequencing CTA preparation: when CTA601 has to be attended, what happens when a registered evaluation date is pushed, and which scored outputs justify registering.

questions.question: A candidate is laying out a 90-day plan and has not yet attended the Prepare for your Technical Architect Certification course. What does the CTA601 course page say about timing?
options: Students should attend this course at least four months before they plan to register for the Architect Evaluation
Students should attend the course during the two to four weeks between registering for the evaluation and sitting it
Students must attend the course before earning the Application Architect credential
Students attend the course after passing the Review Board Exam, as preparation for certification maintenance
questions.explanation: The course page states that students should attend at least four months before they plan to register for the Architect Evaluation, which is why the course sits early in the calendar. The two to four week window is the readiness requirement attached to registration itself, so it cannot double as the training window. If the course is not behind the candidate, the registration date moves rather than the course.

questions.question: A candidate registers for the Architect Evaluation and then asks the program team to push the date out by six weeks. According to the Architect Program FAQ, what happens?
options: The evaluation moves to the new date with no penalty
The retake fee is applied and the original slot is held
The Architect Evaluation will be canceled and the candidate will need to re-register when they are prepared
The evaluation converts into a Review Board Exam slot in the new month
questions.explanation: The FAQ states that candidates must be ready to appear for the evaluation two to four weeks after registering, and that requesting to push the date cancels the evaluation so the candidate must re-register when prepared. That is why this lesson asks for a written stop rule instead of a hopeful registration date. Reading the rule the other way costs six months after an unsuccessful evaluation.

questions.question: Which scored output does the lesson treat as the gate that has to be in the log before registering for the evaluation?
options: A finished set of study notes covering all seven outline areas
A scored mock board in which a person who will not help you sat through the presentation and put the questions to you
A completed Architect Journey Trailmix with every badge earned
A written summary of the five Well-Architected Framework pillars
questions.explanation: The lesson defines the readiness gate as three scored outputs, and the mock board is the one that tests the presentation and the defense under questioning. A complete constraint table on an unseen scenario and a full artifact set produced inside the clock complete the gate. Notes and badge counts are inputs to the plan, not evidence that it worked.
